editorial.headline: A Nationally Open Personal-Services Activity, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This broad personal-services activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration today.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 96900** covers an unusually broad field of personal services. At the household end, it includes cooking, washing, cleaning and ironing performed in households. Its social strand includes companion and dating services, speed-networking activities and marriage bureaux, alongside astrology, spiritual activity, genealogy organisations and house-sitting. It also reaches animal-related services: pet boarding, grooming, care, guarding and training; shelters for abandoned animals; and horse whispering. The scope is deliberately expansive rather than centred on one profession, bringing together everyday assistance, personal occasions and specialised small services under one activity.

That breadth continues in its operational examples. Shoe shining, porter work and valet parking sit beside coin-operated personal-service machines, including photo booths, weighing machines, blood-pressure machines and coin-operated lockers. The activity also covers photo booths and printing machines that make photographs from electronic records such as phones, memory cards and flash drives; temporary decorative tattoo work using biological substances such as henna; and private-event organisation other than funerals, including wedding planning, birthday parties, bachelor and bachelorette parties, and annual celebrations. It is an activity defined by the range of personal-facing services it brings together.

At the national level, the status is open and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. Registration is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. This gives the activity a clear national footing across every scale listed in the record, whether the business is built around household assistance, animal care, personal-service machines or private-event organisation. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nationally, foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership for this activity.

Bali is the decisive exception. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. The record marks it blocked by risk class: at the Besar scale, every scope carries Low or Medium-Low OSS risk, placing it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The stated moratorium date is 13 May 2026, with Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP given as the source. National openness and a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling do not create a PMA registration route for this activity in Bali.
